triplets.head: LSM-Tree paper
triplets.tail: Dieter Gawlick's database research group at Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC), Mountain View, California

triplets.head: LSM-Tree paper
triplets.tail: Traditional B-tree indexes cause catastrophic random I/O for write-heavy workloads (e.g., TPC-A benchmark)

triplets.head: LSM-Tree paper
triplets.tail: Multi-component tree with memory-resident C0 and disk-resident C1, C2, etc.

triplets.head: LSM-Tree paper
triplets.tail: Rolling merge: conceptual cursor circulates through C0/C1 key space, reads multi-page blocks from C1, merges with C0 entries, writes new merged blocks sequentially

triplets.head: LSM-Tree paper
triplets.tail: k components (C0...Ck) with sizes in geometric progression (ratio r); paper suggests ≤3 components in practice

triplets.head: LSM-Tree paper
triplets.tail: Orders of magnitude lower insert cost than B-trees; reads slightly less efficient (must check multiple components)

triplets.head: B-tree
triplets.tail: Dominant baseline index structure that LSM-Tree aimed to improve upon for write-heavy workloads

triplets.head: Log-Structured File System
triplets.tail: Direct conceptual inspiration for LSM-Tree (sequential-only writes to disk)

triplets.head: Log-Structured File System
triplets.tail: SOSP '91 (13th ACM Symposium on Operating Systems Principles), October 1991

triplets.head: Log-Structured File System
triplets.tail: ACM TOCS, Vol. 10, No. 1, pp. 26–52, February 1992

triplets.head: Log-Structured File System
triplets.tail: Applied concept to file system; LSM-Tree applied it to index structures

triplets.head: Differential File
triplets.tail: Earliest deferred-write concept; LSM-Tree synthesized this idea

triplets.head: Selective Deferred Index Maintenance
triplets.tail: In-memory cache not authoritative for reads

triplets.head: Time-Split B-Tree (TSB-Tree)
triplets.tail: Prior write-optimization approach for multiversion data

triplets.head: Time-Split B-Tree (TSB-Tree)
triplets.tail: ACM SIGMOD 1989, Portland, OR, pp. 315–324; ACM SIGMOD 1990, Atlantic City, NJ, pp. 353–363

triplets.head: MD/OD R-Tree
triplets.tail: Prior write-optimization approach using vacuum cleaner daemon

triplets.head: MD/OD R-Tree
triplets.tail: Same limitation as TSB-tree: no guaranteed memory-resident initial component

triplets.head: Bounded Disorder File
triplets.tail: Prior write-optimization approach with hybrid hashing/tree indexing

triplets.head: SB-Tree
triplets.tail: Patrick O'Neil's own prior work on index-sequential structure

triplets.head: Five Minute Rule
triplets.tail: Economic framework for trading memory for disk accesses; synthesized into LSM-Tree design

triplets.head: LSM-Tree paper
triplets.tail: Synthesized Differential File (deferred writes), LFS (sequential-only writes), and Five Minute Rule (economic tradeoff), while guaranteeing a fully memory-resident, authoritative C0 component with efficient rolling merge

triplets.head: Generation 0: Rolling Merge / Classic Leveling
triplets.tail: O'Neil et al., 'The Log-Structured Merge-Tree (LSM-Tree)', Acta Informatica, Vol. 33, No. 4, pp. 351–385, 1996

triplets.head: Generation 0: Rolling Merge / Classic Leveling
triplets.tail: One sorted run per level; full rolling merge between C0 and C1; formally the leveling merge policy

triplets.head: Generation 1: Size-Tiered Compaction / Tiering
triplets.tail: Chang, Dean, Ghemawat et al., 'Bigtable: A Distributed Storage System for Structured Data', OSDI '06, pp. 205–218, 2006

triplets.head: Generation 1: Size-Tiered Compaction / Tiering
triplets.tail: Minor compaction (MemTable flush) and major compaction (merge all SSTables); multiple sorted runs per level; lower write amplification, higher read/space amplification

triplets.head: Generation 1: Size-Tiered Compaction / Tiering
triplets.tail: HBase, Cassandra (as Size-Tiered Compaction Strategy / STCS)

triplets.head: Generation 2: Leveled Compaction
triplets.tail: File-granular partial merge; levels L0–Ln with 10× size ratio; each level beyond L0 has one sorted run partitioned into non-overlapping SSTable files

triplets.head: Generation 2: Leveled Compaction
triplets.tail: Low read/space amplification, high write amplification (~10× per level)

triplets.head: Generation 3: Spring-and-Gear Merge Scheduler
triplets.tail: Sears and Ramakrishnan, 'bLSM: A General Purpose Log Structured Merge Tree', ACM SIGMOD 2012, pp. 217–228

triplets.head: Generation 3: Spring-and-Gear Merge Scheduler
triplets.tail: Latency-bounded merge scheduling; steady progress without blocking writes; introduced read fanout metric

triplets.head: Generation 4: Key-Value Separation
triplets.tail: Lu, Pillai, Arpaci-Dusseau, Arpaci-Dusseau, 'WiscKey: Separating Keys from Values in SSD-Conscious Storage', USENIX FAST '16, pp. 133–148

triplets.head: Generation 4: Key-Value Separation
triplets.tail: Keys in LSM-tree, large values in separate append-only vLog; compaction only sorts keys; 2.5×–111× faster than LevelDB

triplets.head: Generation 5: Fragmented LSM-Tree / Guards
triplets.tail: Raju, Kadekodi, Chidambaram, Abraham, 'PebblesDB: Building Key-Value Stores using Fragmented Log-Structured Merge Trees', ACM SOSP '17, pp. 497–514

triplets.head: Generation 5: Fragmented LSM-Tree / Guards
triplets.tail: Guards partition key space; data inserted without rewriting existing data; up to 6.7× less write amplification than RocksDB

triplets.head: Generation 6: Lazy Leveling & Fluid LSM-Tree
triplets.tail: Dayan and Idreos, 'Dostoevsky: Better Space-Time Trade-Offs for LSM-Tree Based Key-Value Stores via Adaptive Removal of Superfluous Merging', ACM SIGMOD '18

triplets.head: Generation 6: Lazy Leveling & Fluid LSM-Tree
triplets.tail: Tiering at all levels except largest (which uses leveling); update cost improves from O(T·L) to O(T+L)

triplets.head: Generation 6: Lazy Leveling & Fluid LSM-Tree
triplets.tail: Parameters Z (max runs at largest level) and K (max runs at other levels); morphs continuously between leveling, lazy leveling, and tiering

triplets.head: Generation 7: LSM-Bush & Wacky Continuum
triplets.tail: Dayan and Idreos, 'The Log-Structured Merge-Bush & the Wacky Continuum', ACM SIGMOD '19, pp. 449–466

triplets.head: Generation 7: LSM-Bush & Wacky Continuum
triplets.tail: Different size ratios at different levels; bushy tree structure; Capped Lazy Leveling (CLL); write cost scaling of O(log log N)

triplets.head: Generation 8: Formal Compaction Design Space
triplets.tail: Sarkar, Staratzis, Zhu, Athanassoulis, 'Constructing and Analyzing the LSM Compaction Design Space', PVLDB, Vol. 14, No. 11, pp. 2216–2229, 2021

triplets.head: Generation 8: Formal Compaction Design Space
triplets.tail: Four orthogonal design primitives: compaction trigger, data layout, compaction granularity, data movement policy; evaluates 10 compaction strategies

triplets.head: Generation 9: Spooky
triplets.tail: Dayan, Weiss, Dashevsky, Pan, Bortnikov, Twitto, 'Spooky: Granulating LSM-Tree Compactions Correctly', PVLDB, Vol. 15, No. 11, pp. 3071–3084, 2022

triplets.head: Generation 9: Spooky
triplets.tail: Addresses flaws in both Full Merge and Partial Merge; partitions data at largest level into equally sized files; >2× improvements in both space and write amplification

triplets.head: Generation 10: Moose
triplets.tail: Liu, Wang, Mo, Luo, 'Structural Designs Meet Optimality: Exploring Optimized LSM-tree Structures in a Colossal Configuration Space', PACMMOD/SIGMOD, Vol. 2, No. 3, Article 175, June 2024

triplets.head: Generation 10: Moose
triplets.tail: Per-level independent configuration of layout, size ratio, buffer size, Bloom filter; cost model-driven optimizer

triplets.head: Generation 11: EcoTune
triplets.tail: Wang, Qiu, Yuan, Zhang, 'Rethinking The Compaction Policies in LSM-trees', PACMMOD/SIGMOD, Vol. 3, No. 3, Article 207, June 2025

triplets.head: Generation 11: EcoTune
triplets.tail: Three-level analytical model; query-stream-dependent compaction strategy adapting to actual workload distribution

triplets.head: FIFO Compaction
triplets.tail: RocksDB engineering implementation (~2014–2015), no formal paper

triplets.head: FIFO Compaction
triplets.tail: Oldest SSTable files dropped when threshold exceeded; no merging; for cache-like/TTL workloads

triplets.head: Monkey
triplets.tail: Dayan and Idreos, 'Monkey: Optimal Navigable Key-Value Store', ACM SIGMOD 2017, pp. 79–94

triplets.head: Monkey
triplets.tail: Optimal Bloom filter allocation across LSM-tree levels

triplets.head: Mao et al. Survey

triplets.tail: Dong, Kryczka, Jin, Stumm, 'RocksDB: Evolution of Development Priorities in a Key-value Store Serving Large-scale Applications', ACM TOS, Vol. 17, No. 4, pp. 1–32, 2021; also USENIX FAST '21

triplets.head: Compaction strategy evolution
triplets.tail: Theory to practice: two canonical policies (leveling, tiering)

triplets.head: Compaction strategy evolution
triplets.tail: Engineering optimizations: latency scheduling, KV separation, fragmentation

triplets.head: Compaction strategy evolution
triplets.tail: Theoretical unification: formal design space, hybrid strategies proven superior

triplets.head: Compaction strategy evolution
triplets.tail: Automated optimization: colossal configuration spaces, workload-adaptive compaction

triplets.head: RocksDB
triplets.tail: Leveled Compaction (called Level Compaction; technically Tiered+Leveled hybrid with L0 tiered and L1+ leveled)

triplets.head: RocksDB
triplets.tail: Dong et al., ACM TOS Vol. 17(4), 2021; USENIX FAST '21

triplets.head: Apache Cassandra
triplets.tail: Unified Compaction Strategy (UCS), introduced via CEP-26

triplets.head: Apache Cassandra
triplets.tail: Lakshman and Malik, 'Cassandra: A Decentralized Structured Storage System', ACM SIGOPS OSR, Vol. 44(2), 2010

triplets.head: Apache HBase
triplets.tail: Size-Tiered (minor compaction merges subset of HFiles; major compaction merges all HFiles in a region)

triplets.head: TiKV
triplets.tail: Titan plugin for key-value separation (WiscKey concept), disabled by default

triplets.head: Pebble (CockroachDB)
triplets.tail: Value separation optimization added in v25.3+

triplets.head: YugabyteDB (DocDB)
triplets.tail: Size-Tiered, single level (all SST files in L0)

triplets.head: YugabyteDB (DocDB)
triplets.tail: YB-TServer manages multiple compaction queues with throttling to prevent compaction storms

triplets.head: BadgerDB
triplets.tail: Leveled Compaction for key-only LSM-tree; values garbage-collected separately from value log

triplets.head: InfluxDB (TSM Engine)
triplets.tail: Time Structured Merge Tree (TSM), an LSM variant optimized for time-series

triplets.head: InfluxDB (TSM Engine)
triplets.tail: Level-based compaction with 4 levels (L1 flushed from cache → L2 → L3 → L4 full compaction)

triplets.head: ArangoDB
triplets.tail: Leveled Compaction (inherits RocksDB defaults; 7 LSM levels; lower levels uncompressed)

triplets.head: MyRocks
triplets.tail: Also available in MariaDB and Percona Server for MySQL

triplets.head: MongoDB (WiredTiger)
triplets.tail: B-tree (default) / LSM-tree (optional); WiredTiger supports both modes

triplets.head: MongoDB (WiredTiger)
triplets.tail: B-tree (not LSM-tree by default); LSM mode uses size-tiered style merging when enabled

triplets.head: FoundationDB
triplets.tail: B-tree (SQLite-derived, SSD engine) / Memory engine (not LSM-tree)

triplets.head: bLSM

triplets.head: bLSM
triplets.tail: Spring-and-Gear merge scheduler that bounds write latency without impacting throughput

triplets.head: bLSM
triplets.tail: None found; cited as related work in many papers but no independent study re-implements and benchmarks it head-to-head

triplets.head: bLSM
triplets.relation: reason for lack of third-party evaluation
triplets.tail: Built on custom codebase (not RocksDB); Spring-and-Gear concept subsumed by SILK and later work, so researchers compare against SILK instead
